rv.q: The production sits in limbo between storytelling and drama, even as it remains a shameful and important reminder of a neglected period of British history.

In the aftermath of this “mutiny”, ringleaders were strapped to the fronts of cannon and blown up, often in the presence of their fellow rebels. Moorjani (who is nonbinary) takes on the role of a rebel charged by a British Army officer (Jonathan Oldfield, who co-directs) to tell the story of the uprising.
Moorjani's play is beautifully written, full of a lyrical sense of the beauty of India and its culture.

cn.t: A two-sided examination of colonial brutality in 1857 India earns mixed reviews, with critics divided on whether its ambitious structure successfully illuminates both perspectives or merely dilutes dramatic impact.
